_doc: Meerkat SLO and alert definitions (Plan 44 Phase 4 WP-4C). JSON so validation stays dependency-free. Full schema + rationale live in deploy/observability/README.md. This file is the INPUT an operator loads into whatever alerting stack exists; this repo hosts no scraper, evaluator, dashboard, or pager (founder-ops). Every objective derives from a metric the services emit (derivesFrom.metric), a synthetic in ./synthetics (derivesFrom.probe), or a structured NDJSON event (derivesFrom.logEvent). An objective whose signal does not exist yet is status pending_signal (missing emitter named) or founder_ops (backup/proof infra not hosted here); none are faked. Zero-knowledge: no SLO reads a relay field beyond {ok,connections}, metric labels are static (service/store/kind/outcome), and there is no cross-service trace.

objectives.title: Relay /healthz zero-knowledge shape
objectives.description: The relay liveness endpoint returns EXACTLY {ok, connections}. A third field is a metadata-privacy regression, treated as an incident, not a degradation.

probe.note: The probe FAILS (exit 2) the moment any key other than ok/connections appears, or the CORS header the web selector depends on is missing.

objectives.title: Relay connection + envelope forwarding availability
objectives.description: The public relay answers /healthz and accepts WebSocket upgrades.

probe.note: Availability is measured by the same public probe (a shaped 200 == available). The relay emits no private metric by design, so the probe is the only signal.

objectives.title: Stateful service readiness availability
objectives.description: Each stateful service (humanity, persona, hosted, directory, community) reports ready via /readyz. Availability is the ratio of ready (200) probe results.

probe.note: The readyz probe walks every service's public /readyz. There is no readyz success COUNTER on the private registry yet, so the synthetic is the availability signal. If a readyz-outcome counter is later added, repoint derivesFrom.metric.

objectives.title: Readiness flap rate
objectives.description: A service that oscillates ready<->not-ready churns the orchestrator and hides a real dependency problem behind restarts. Page on excessive transitions.

probe.note: Flap == count of ready-state transitions between consecutive probe results over the window. Derived by the alerting stack from the probe's NDJSON ready field; no metric exists for this (a readiness gauge is intentionally NOT exported to keep the private registry free of a per-scrape readiness series).

objectives.title: PostgreSQL pool saturation
objectives.description: Waiting clients on the pg pool mean requests are queuing for a connection. Sustained waiting is the leading indicator of the statement/lock timeouts below.

metric.name: meerkat_postgres_pool_connections
metric.note: Emitted by every postgres-mode service. The community node emits the suffixed variants meerkat_postgres_pool_connections_community and _moderation; alert on all three families. states are total/idle/waiting.

alerts.condition: waiting > 0 for 15m OR (idle == 0 AND waiting > 0) for 5m

objectives.title: Shadow comparator divergence during a migration window
objectives.description: In shadow mode the file primary is mirrored to the postgres shadow and results are compared. ANY divergence during a cutover window is an incident: the two backends disagree on state that gates security or lifecycle. The objective is ZERO.

metric.name: meerkat_shadow_events_total
metric.note: Emitted by the community and persona bins as a counter with labels service/store/kind. kind is one of agreement|divergence|shadow_fault. Alert on any increase of the kind=divergence series. kind=shadow_fault (the shadow was slow or threw) is a ticket, not a page, but a rising fault rate blinds the comparator and should be investigated.

alerts.condition: increase(kind=divergence) > 0 during any active migration window

objectives.title: Referenced object missing (page)
objectives.description: A ledger row references an object key whose store object is ABSENT. A user path for that object returns an exact unavailable state; the byte must be restored or the reference repaired. This is a page.

logEvent.note: The object reconciler (src/object-reconciler.ts) classifies each finding with a typed outcome including referenced_missing. NO Prometheus counter for reconciler outcomes is wired, AND no production worker currently runs the reconciler on a schedule. Until a reconciler worker bin exists and either logs a reconcile_finding NDJSON event or increments a counter, this alert cannot fire.

objectives.title: Orphan object sweeps (ticket)
objectives.description: An orphan is a store object with no ledger row. Quarantine and eventual sweep is the designed, safe outcome; a rising rate is a ticket to investigate the producer, not a page.

logEvent.note: Outcomes orphan_quarantined and orphan_swept from src/object-reconciler.ts. Same pending_signal caveat as reconciler-referenced-missing: no worker runs it yet.

objectives.title: Object deletion job poison (page)
objectives.description: The deletion queue is the ONLY component that removes managed bytes. A poisoned deletion job is a byte that the system decided to delete but could not, repeatedly. A non-zero poison count is a page: bytes are stuck in a half-deleted state.

logEvent.note: src/object-deletion-jobs-*.ts implement a poison() transition and listPoison(). NO metric exports the poison count and no production deletion worker bin runs the queue yet. Until a deletion worker exists and exports the poison count (a collect() gauge over listPoison length is the natural wiring) or logs a deletion_poison event, this alert cannot fire.

objectives.title: Confirmed backup freshness
objectives.description: 100% of the confirmed-backup window is covered by a backup that has a recent restore proof. A backup without a restore proof is NOT healthy (NC-44.3). The freshness SIGNAL is real (Plan 44 WP-5A): a synthetic reads the latest verified ops.backup_restore_proofs row. Provisioning the underlying provider backups and WAL archiving is still founder-ops; this objective measures whether a recorded restore proof is recent, not whether the provider job ran.

probe.note: The probe reads the latest VERIFIED restore proof through the read-only observer credential and FAILS (exit 2) on a missing or stale proof, degrades (exit 1) when the recorded RPO exceeds maxRpoSeconds. Thresholds above are parsed directly from this objective, no new dependency.

alerts.condition: no verified restore proof within maxProofAgeSeconds (probe exit 2)

objectives.title: Weekly restore proof gate
objectives.description: A weekly restore job proves the backup restores. A failed or missing weekly restore proof fails the release health gate and pages.

logEvent.note: The restore-smoke TOOL exists (Plan 44 WP-5A: meerkat-postgres-backup --restore-smoke records a proof, and backup-freshness reads it). This objective stays founder_ops because it asserts the weekly restore job is actually RUN against a real provider backup on a schedule; a tool that exists is not a drill that ran. When founder-ops schedules the weekly restore-smoke, its recorded proofs make backup-freshness fresh.

alerts.condition: weekly restore smoke fails or is absent
